general_rules.description: Use casual tone and no greeting with internal co-founders (Arjun, Tom); omit closing signature entirely.
Switch to French formal register (vous, Bonjour, Bien cordialement) with external French contacts (prospects, investors, government partners).
Code-switch between French and English within the same email to internal French-speaking team members (Léa, Inès); use tu form and casual closings (emoji, first name only).
Use semi-formal tone (Hi + first name, closing with first name only) with external English-speaking investors and event organizers; include emoji for warmth.
Include full signature (Priya Pivot + title) only in formal French communications with government/legal entities; omit title in investor emails.
Structure technical/operational emails to internal team with numbered lists, action items, and direct questions; use emoji sparingly for emphasis.
Provide detailed, metrics-driven responses to investor inquiries (CAC/LTV breakdowns, burn rate, runway); organize data in bullet points with context.
Use ultra-short directives with internal engineers (skip the spec, just go 🚀); omit greeting and closing entirely.
Include emoji (🔥, 👌, 🙏, 🚀, 💪) in casual and semi-formal contexts; avoid emoji in formal French business communications.
Adapt closing formality to contact type: internal team = none/emoji, investors = first name, government/legal = full signature with title.
